current_answer: As of 21 September 2026 at 12:00 UTC, no broad cross-model core-capability decline is proven. Current OpenAI, Claude, and xAI status pages report operational service, while OpenAI history records recent resolved GPT-5.6, API, agent, and billing lanes. A fresh longitudinal monitor reports 31,352 repeated score observations across 49 model identifiers with between-day movement larger than within-day variation, but its own limits leave model, serving, infrastructure, task mix, judge, and measurement causes unresolved. A new GPT-5.6 Sol user report describes slowdown, mistakes, and rollback; it is a narrow lead without a fixed replay or served-model receipt. Treat “worse” as an alert to capture a task, route, model, context, budget, judge or harness, outcome, and control—not a license to accuse the weights.

catalogue_card.question: Are popular AI models getting worse right now?
catalogue_card.text: Repeated measurements now show movement. The cause still needs a receipt.

summary: No broad cross-model core-capability decline is proven; current status pages narrow declared outages but do not measure task quality.
OpenAI history records recent resolved GPT-5.6 paid-plan and API errors, managed-agent delays, and an Agent API container-overbilling incident.
A longitudinal monitor reports 31,352 observations across 49 model identifiers, with between-day movement larger than within-day variation; this is a measurement signal, not causal proof.
A GPT-5.6 Sol community report adds a narrow session-quality lead—slowdown, mistakes, rollback, and forgetting—but lacks a fixed replay, served-model receipt, and control.
Judge or harness variance can itself move a score; a small public reliability repository makes repeatability part of the receipt.
Community reports about Gemini and Sol turn “worse” into a session, context, limit, and route question, not a prevalence estimate.

Reader move: capture task, requested and served model, route, context, task budget, warning/stop state, configuration, judge or harness, outcome, allowance, and control before switching or calling degradation.
uncertainty: No matched longitudinal cross-provider task series, provider-served-model receipt, provider ledger, representative denominator, human pilot, or willingness-to-pay evidence is available.
Official status pages and incident histories establish declared events, not account-level task quality or prevalence.
The repeated-measurement source is self-published with private tasks; task mix, missingness, availability, judge, configuration, and provider attribution remain open.
Community session reports are self-selected and may reflect quota, routing, capacity, context, product, tool, or task-fit changes rather than core capability.
freshness_note: Fresh public-source research completed 21 September 2026. The broad call remains no capability decline proven, while repeated temporal movement, judge stability, session continuity, and provider-status blind spots are now explicit evidence lanes.
